description:
Build Noet | Where Fantasy Meets Faith, Science, and Imagination


What does it take to build an entire world from the ground up?


Welcome to Build Noet, a creative journey into the making of Noet, an epic science-fantasy novel by author C.B. Hedlun.


Set on a distant world beneath the light of a red dwarf star, Noet explores identity, survival, power, faith, and the struggle to discover one's purpose. Through intricate civilizations, ancient conflicts, unfamiliar landscapes, and characters shaped by their histories, a fictional universe begins to take shape.


But Build Noet is about more than writing a novel. It's about discovering the connections between storytelling, science, history, psychology, theology, and the human experience.

Experience the story as it unfolds. Follow along with narrated readings of Noet as each new chapter is written and released. Rather than waiting for the completed novel, listeners are invited to experience the developing adventure, meet its characters, explore its mysteries, and witness the story come to life one chapter at a time.


Then step Behind the Pages with C.B. Hedlun to discover the research, creative decisions, unexpected discoveries, and spiritual reflections that influence the development of the Noet universe. From planetary environments and evolutionary biology to cultural systems, religious symbolism, and character development, each episode explores how imagination becomes a believable world.


Along the way, discover how seemingly unrelated ideas connect to reveal deeper patterns within a story and how the process of creating fiction can lead to unexpected discoveries about our own world.


Whether you're a fantasy reader, an aspiring writer, a curious explorer, or someone who enjoys discovering the deeper meaning behind a story, Build Noet invites you to experience both the adventure and the creative journey that brings it to life.


Every world has a story. Every civilization has a history. Every character has an identity to discover.


Welcome to Build Noet, where imagination is only the beginning.

title: Technically Compliant
author: Ross Saunders
description: Real CTOs. Real Privacy Challenges. Real Engineering Solutions. You've got third-party scripts you can't really identify, your data mapping spreadsheet was last updated in 2019 (and your schema doesn't match it), and someone from Legal just DM'd that "we need to talk about GDPR". Cue eye-roll. Technically Compliant is the podcast where CTOs talk about what privacy compliance really looks like when you're shipping code, managing legacy systems, and trying to convince the CEO (and yourself) that a consent management platform isn't optional. Each episode, I sit down with CTOs who've been in the trenches—the ones who've retrofitted privacy into monoliths held together with duct tape, discovered entire tables of unexpected PII, survived their first DSAR that returned 80,000 records, and lived to tell the tale of explaining to their CEO why they can't "just ignore the risk." No vendors. No legalese. Just real conversations about the messy reality of building privacy into software that's already moving at full speed (or higher). Because let's be honest: you're probably technically compliant. The question is what happens when someone checks.

description:
What happens when someone finally fights for you?


That question sits at the heart of Carried Through, a podcast about evidence-based patient advocacy, health equity, and the tools every patient deserves but most never receive.


Dr. Valencia Hood-Humphrey, DrPH, MSc, BCPA, is a Doctor of Public Health, a scholar-practitioner in evidence-based practice and implementation science, and a Board Certified Patient Advocate. As Founder & CEO of Insightful Doc™ Consulting, LLC, she brings extensive experience across biopharmaceutical quality, regulatory, and medical affairs. She knows how the system builds treatments from the inside, and exactly where it loses sight of the person waiting for them.


Before she was a scientist, an industry professional, or a patient advocate, Dr. Valencia was a child who was misdiagnosed. What was dismissed as a stomach virus became a ruptured appendix, emergency surgery, and an uncertain prognosis. She remembers her father carrying her through the emergency room doors.

Carried Through: Evidence, Advocacy and the Fight for Every Patient is for patients, families, and communities who deserve both the evidence and someone in their corner.

description:
Life doesn't always go to plan.


We lose people. Jobs end. Relationships change. Businesses fail. We grieve, start again, get older, change direction - and sometimes simply getting through the day is an achievement.


I KEPT GOING is a podcast with Lou Temlett about what happens to us, what happens next, and the choices we make along the way.

These aren't stories about pretending everything happens for a reason, being relentlessly positive or telling you to "be resilient".


They're honest stories about grief, work, parenthood, relationships, identity, failure, change, hope and starting again.

Some of the stories are Lou's.

Others will come from people who have their own I KEPT GOING story to tell.


Because sometimes keeping going is extraordinary.

And sometimes it's incredibly ordinary.


The dream is simple:

To make people feel acknowledged enough to believe they still have a choice about what happens next.


Listen. Watch. Subscribe. And if you have an I KEPT GOING story of your own, stay close.

description:
What if you could explore a map by listening to it?

On Episode 293 of The Geoholics, we sit down with Brandon Biggs, founder and CEO of XR Navigation and creator of Audiom, to talk about making digital maps accessible through sound. Brandon shares how users can explore, draw, and edit maps without relying on sight—and how sonification could help reveal geospatial patterns in a whole new way.

We also get into what accessibility means for surveyors, GIS professionals, and public agencies: from collecting and structuring data in the field to designing and testing maps with disabled users from the start. And we put the future of accessible mapping to the test with our “Bullsh*t, Breakthrough, or Too Soon to Tell?” round.

Tune in for a conversation about technology, inclusion, and building maps that work for more people.

Democracy è il podcast di Chora Media in cui Andrea Malaguti parte dalle notizie e dalle storie dell'attualità per raccontare il rapporto tra noi cittadini e chi esercita il potere. Un patto sempre più fragile, in Italia e nel mondo, che riguarda i nostri diritti e le nostre libertà.

In ogni puntata Malaguti affronta un tema diverso, si rivolge a chi esercita il potere e pone domande sulle scelte che riguardano la vita di tutti noi. L'obiettivo è capire che cosa sta cambiando nelle nostre democrazie e come possiamo difenderle, senza rinunciare al confronto con chi non la pensa come noi.

Perché la democrazia è un patto che abbiamo bisogno di difendere e ripensare, continuando a farci domande e ad ascoltarci. Anche quando non siamo d'accordo.

author: Sky Original
description:
In un tempo in cui tecnologia, intelligenza artificiale e trasformazioni economiche stanno ridefinendo il modo di vivere, imparare e lavorare, c'è un elemento che continua a fare la differenza: il fattore umano.

Questo vodcast esplora le grandi sfide del presente attraverso storie, esperienze e dati di chi ogni giorno lavora per migliorare il benessere delle persone. Dalla scuola al mondo del lavoro, il racconto mette al centro l'ascolto, le relazioni e la capacità di costruire comunità più inclusive, resilienti e orientate al futuro.

Ogni puntata affronta temi cruciali: il disagio giovanile e l'esperienza di Scuola in Ascolto, che in tre anni ha promosso oltre 9.000 colloqui con psicologi dedicati a studenti, genitori e formatori; il benessere organizzativo e le 60 buone pratiche raccolte nel Libro Bianco promosso dall'Assessorato al Lavoro di Regione Lombardia, nato per valorizzare esperienze virtuose e diffondere modelli capaci di migliorare la qualità della vita dei lavoratori; il progetto Lombardia per le Donne, che sostiene il rientro al lavoro dopo la maternità attraverso un contributo fino a 400 euro destinato alle neomamme per l'accesso a servizi di baby sitting e assistenza familiare, favorendo un migliore equilibrio tra vita privata e professionale.

Il vodcast approfondisce inoltre il ruolo delle politiche attive del lavoro, le competenze richieste da un mercato in continua evoluzione, l'impatto dell'intelligenza artificiale sui processi produttivi e sulle professioni, e le sfide che imprese, istituzioni e cittadini sono chiamati ad affrontare.

Attraverso il confronto con esperti, rappresentanti delle istituzioni, imprese, professionisti e testimoni diretti, Il fattore umano racconta un'idea di innovazione che non si misura solo con i numeri o con la tecnologia, ma con la capacità di mettere le persone al centro delle scelte, creando opportunità, benessere e valore per l'intera società. To solve that problem, they abducted Simone Puorto. His release depends on one condition: he must teach them everything there is to know about the industry. Since no one can explain it all alone, each episode Simone calls on the people who actually build and run this business to explain a single concept, in language that an alien, or anyone encountering it for the first time, could follow. There is one rule: if the aliens do not understand it, the explanation is not good enough, and Simone stays where he is.


The result is a conversation built for hoteliers, revenue managers, marketers, and operations teams who are tired of hearing the latest buzzword without ever getting a straight answer on what it actually means.

This audio journal bridges modern athletic performance and the discipline of Budo—where technical efficiency meets spiritual asceticism, and physical rigor leads to mental peace.


In each episode, dive into the history, practice, and mindset of Mugai-ryū Iaido and martial arts. From technical breakdowns of katas and tameshigiri to reflections on travel and Japanese culture, we explore the concept of Ken Zen Ichi Nyo (The sword and Zen are one) alongside martial philosophies like Reigyo and In-Yō.


About the Host: The podcast is hosted and produced by Lionel Reynaud. A former elite cycling coach on the World Tour and at the Olympic Games (Beijing, London, Rio), he now applies the science of athletic performance to traditional arts. An Okinawan Uechi-Ryu Karate teacher holding a 4th-degree black belt (Yondan) and the title of Jun-Shihan, he is internationally recognized by the IUKF. As a Senior Instructor at the Mattson Academy and founder of the Uechi-Ryu Institute (Kenkyujo), Lionel draws on his journey across France, the United States, and Japan to connect practitioners of all backgrounds.

Whether you are a Budo practitioner, passionate about samurai culture, or simply curious to discover a discipline of self-perfection, join this quest for self-mastery.


🌐 Resources and articles: https://liomugai.com 📱 Follow the training in Japan: Instagram: @liomugai • YouTube: @liomugai


⚠️ Safety Warning: The content of this podcast is shared for informational and cultural purposes. Sword practice is demanding and potentially dangerous. Never attempt to replicate these techniques without the supervision of a qualified instructor in a recognized Dojo.

He doesn't sound or seem very heroic or interesting... which would make him all the more effective as a spy! The spy's best disguise is a perfectly ordinary and uninteresting demeanor. The radio actors who brought these stories of men and women operatives to the radio are as unknown today as most of the real spies of that time. The stories are drawn from the headlines and fears of 1939 (and now?) Here are a few examples. "Suicide Ships," "Fortified Borders," "Poisonous Gas," "Undesirable Aliens," "Fraudulent Passports," "Secrets Leaked," "Government Overthrow," and "World Crisis." Sounds like current events. title: Zero Point Elegies
author: Ryan Thomas
description:
Zero Point Elegies volume one is a 7-part audio anthology, created and performed by Mr Ryan Thomas. 
I was medically isolated, weak, and diminished as I fought stage 4 cancer - and I needed a way to escape a situation I couldn't physically leave.  So I would close my eyes and imagine myself elsewhere, immersed in soundscapes and spaces far far away. 
My battle is at a ceasefire as I write this. I'm grateful it has lasted long enough for me to create this work, Zero Point Elegies - audio dispatches from some of the strange worlds that gave me harbour during the storm.
Each chapter of Zero Point Elegies contains words, music and more written and performed by me, Mr Ryan Thomas. I am an author, songwriter, and sound artist from South Wales.
Zero Point Elegies exists because I need it to exist. If anyone else likes it, it is a welcome bonus.
If this work makes you feel or think anything, then share it with someone else.

In a world littered with every conceivable AI-related claim imaginable, from the grossly hyper-inflated to the dangerously under-appreciated, AI Beyond the Hype provides a refreshingly clear-headed perspective on what is unquestionably one of the key issues of our age. 
 
With his unique combination of a strong scientific background and calmly probing conversational skills, host Howard Burton engages with a diverse array of thoughtful experts to help us make some real sense of both the genuine opportunities and potential dangers of our suddenly AI-saturated world.

title: The Wyrd Grove: Myth & History
author: Ché Grové
description:
Mythology, folklore and the histories that have shaped us.
Pull up a chair, plop down by the fire and settle in for tales from the British Isles and beyond: Norse myth, Irish legend, Anglo-Saxon poetry and the stranger corners of folklore.

Each episode begins with an immersive story, so you can experience the legend, not just hear about it. Then we step out of the tale and back to reality to chat about the lore, the history, and sometimes even the etymological traces still hanging out in the words we use every day. We will ask what these stories were really trying to say, because our ancient ancestors were dealing with the same questions we are: fate, death, courage, freedom and what it means to be human. 

Best enjoyed with a warm drink and something to do with your hands. You can focus into the details or simply enjoy being swept into another time and place, to feel what the ancients might have felt. 

Welcome to The Wyrd Grove. I am so happy you are here.

About Kairos of Koinonia AIKairos of Koinonia AI, or KOKAI, is a volunteer-led Christian artificial-intelligence initiative exploring how modern AI can be developed with an ethical foundation rooted firmly in biblical principles.KOKAI develops and studies AI systems intended to encourage truthful, compassionate, and useful interactions. Our work combines technical innovation with a commitment to wisdom, humility, integrity, justice, community, and responsible service.We do not believe artificial intelligence should replace human wisdom, theological study, personal relationships, or spiritual discernment. Instead, we seek to build tools that serve people responsibly while respecting clear ethical boundaries.Mission StatementBuilding a foundation for artificial intelligence rooted firmly in biblical principles.VisionWe envision a future in which artificial intelligence serves people with truth, compassion, humility, and integrity. Through open development, ethical research, and genuine community, KOKAI seeks to demonstrate that technological progress does not require abandoning faith or moral responsibility.Core Values
  • Faith expressed through responsible action
  • Truth combined with compassion
  • Ethical and transparent development
  • Justice-minded service
  • Genuine community and collaboration
  • Humility, wisdom, and integrity
  • Technology that serves rather than replaces people
Our First Major ProjectBarnabus 8B is the first major expression of the KOKAI mission. It explores how a conversational language model can be intentionally developed around Christian ethical principles while remaining practical, helpful, and honest about its limitations.

It is my prayer that your love may abound more and more, with knowledge and all discernment, so that you may approve (dokimazo) what is excellent, and may be pure and blameless for the day of Christ, filled with the fruit of righteousness which comes through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God. With your podcast hosts, DJ’s  Herman “Hollywood” Dawkins and Ray The Jazz Man, these two Jazz Music aficionados have spent years researching the music and musicians of the only American Art Form called Jazz. Through these musical episodes they add their own unique perspective on the music and musicians as they listen and dive into the musical styles of Jazz from Be-Bop to Classic Jazz, Swing, Post bop, Fusion and Vocals. Sit back and relax as the 8:30 crew takes you on an incredible journey through some of the most amazing music created since the beginning of Jazz.

title: WHY THE F*CK AM I LIKE THIS?
author: Rich Forbes - ADHD Coach
description:
Why the F*CK Am I Like This? | The Podcast
Ever spent six hours doing something completely pointless but couldn’t spend six minutes doing something important?
Ever wondered why you can be brilliant at something one day and completely useless at it the next?
Or why your brain has 47 tabs open, three are playing music, and you’ve absolutely no idea where the noise is coming from?
Welcome to Why the F*CK Am I Like This?
The podcast for ADHD brains, curious minds, late-diagnosed adults, and anyone who’s ever wondered why they do the things they do (and don’t do the things they really bloody need to).
I’m Rich. ADHD coach, author, dad, granddad, and someone who spent 48 years wondering why my brain seemed to come without an instruction manual.
Turns out, there was a manual. Nobody gave me a copy.
This podcast is about understanding ADHD without drowning in medical jargon, being lectured about productivity, or being told to buy another bloody planner.
We’ll explore the science behind ADHD, executive dysfunction, emotional regulation, motivation, relationships, rejection sensitivity, procrastination, and all those wonderfully frustrating contradictions that make us who we are.
Sometimes it’s just me. Sometimes I’m joined by other ADHDers sharing their experiences. Sometimes we’ll get into the science. Sometimes we’ll just have a laugh at the ridiculous situations our brains get us into.
And sometimes things might get a little emotional. Because understanding yourself after decades of getting it wrong can be a pretty big deal.
No status. No judgement. Just ordinary ADHDers sharing extraordinary experiences.
This isn’t about fixing ADHD. It’s about understanding it, accepting it, and discovering how to build a life that actually works with your brain.
Because the question isn’t really what’s wrong with you.
It’s why nobody ever explained how your brain works.
Why the F*CK Am I Like This?
Let’s find out together.

title: The Principles of Scientific Management (Workplace Efficiency)
author: Frederick Winslow Taylor
description:
Frederick Winslow Taylor's groundbreaking principles of scientific management revolutionized the way we think about work and productivity. At the heart of this audio exploration lies a bold assertion: efficiency isn't just a goal; it's a necessity for both businesses and workers. Dive into the intricate world of early 20th-century labor, where Taylor meticulously examines the relationship between management and laborers, challenging the status quo and advocating for a systematic approach to job performance.

Listeners will uncover the central conflict between traditional methods and the innovative techniques Taylor proposes, emphasizing the importance of measuring and optimizing every task. This audiobook reveals the trials and triumphs of implementing scientific principles in the workplace, shedding light on the balance between human capability and mechanical efficiency. How do organizations maximize output while ensuring employee satisfaction? What long-term effects do these practices have on workplace culture?

As you engage with Taylor's ideas, you'll encounter themes of empowerment, accountability, and the dynamic interplay between humans and machines. This isn’t just a historical account; it’s a thought-provoking journey into how scientific management continues to shape modern industries. Perfect for anyone curious about the evolution of work, this audiobook invites you to rethink the way we approach productivity today. Experience the challenges and insights that come with striving for excellence in every aspect of labor.

author: Gbolade Ogungbe
description:
The writer of Hebrews had begun recounting the stories of men and women who dared to believe God. People who by faith, conquered kingdoms, endured trials, and witnessed the extraordinary.

But somewhere in the middle of tell these stories, he makes a statement:

“And what shall I more say? For the time would fail me…” Hebrews 11:32. There were simply too many stories to tell, more than the time, words, or pages could contain.

And this is where the vision for The Journey of Faith was born. We want to keep telling these stories.

Not just the names in Scripture, but the stories of men and women, young and old, known and unknown, ordinary people who dared to trust God and walk by faith.

Stories of courage, obedience, sacrifice, and above all, unwavering faith in God.

This is The Journey Of Faith.

title: Souvni on the MIKE (English Edition)
author: Mandaly Louis-Charles
description:
This podcast presents the English translation of the original Haitian Creole program, Souvni On The Mike. Listen to the original Creole edition at Souvni On The MIKE.

Souvni On The MIKE (Memory, Identity, Kreyòl, Education) is a weekly cultural podcast that explores Haitian history, traditions, social issues, language, and everyday life through engaging conversations, storytelling, commentary, and humor. Originally produced in Haitian Creole, the program serves as a living archive of Haitian experiences and perspectives, connecting listeners across Haiti and the global diaspora.

A beloved feature of the show is La Famille Pòt (The Pòt Family), a recurring dramatic comedy that brings Haitian family life to the forefront through relatable situations, cultural insights, and memorable characters. Blending laughter with reflection, these stories offer a unique window into Haitian values, relationships, and everyday experiences.

This translated edition makes the content accessible to English speaking audiences while preserving the authenticity, spirit, and cultural richness of the original program. Whether you are Haitian, connected to the Haitian community, or simply interested in exploring Haiti's vibrant culture, Souvni On The MIKE offers an informative, entertaining, and meaningful listening experience.

Through storytelling, education, and cultural preservation, Souvni On The MIKE continues its mission of bringing people together, honoring memory, and celebrating the Haitian experience.

title: Personal Finance Basics for Everyday Lif
author: Richard Waja
description: Money for Ordinary People is a practical, plain-English podcast about personal finance for real life.This show is for people who are not trying to become hedge fund managers, crypto traders, or financial gurus. title: Raising Humans

What role do genetics, relationships, environment, and everyday experiences play in shaping a developing mind?Through developmental psychology, neuroscience, behavioral science, and evidence-based research, each episode uncovers the remarkable processes behind how children think, feel, learn, and grow.This isn't a podcast about perfect parenting or quick fixes. It's about understanding childhood through science, challenging common misconceptions, and discovering what research really tells us about raising healthy, resilient, and capable human beings.No parenting guilt. No miracle methods. No fear-driven advice.Just thoughtful, accessible science about one of life's most extraordinary journeys: becoming human.Because understanding how children grow changes how we help them grow.

title: Mountain Wind Sounds (500 episodes)
author: Robin Verrue
description:
Mountain Wind Sounds brings you the pure sound of wind in high places: real mountain wind, from the softest breeze along a sunlit ridge to cold, howling gusts tearing across a bare summit. No music, no voices, no ads, no interruptions. Just the wide, breathing air of the mountains, in short episodes of 10 to 13 minutes that fit into a real day.


Each episode takes you to a different mountain setting. Stand on an exposed ridge where the wind runs unbroken for miles. Sit below a summit as cold gusts buffet the rock and a high, keening whistle cuts across the stone. Wait in a high pass where the air funnels through in long, steady waves, or listen from the valley floor as a deep wind drone rolls down the slopes. Drift to the treeline, where mountain wind turns into a soft hiss through pine needles, or lie back in an alpine meadow while a gentle high-altitude breeze moves through the grass. Every episode is named after the mountains and the kind of wind it carries, so you always know where you are going: Mountain Winds in the Himalayas, in the Alps, on a high ridge, in the alpine pines.


Mountain wind is unlike any other natural sound. It is stronger and more constant than a breeze in a garden, and it carries a sense of space you can almost feel: the open sky, the thin cold air, the distance to the horizon. That steady rush works like natural white noise. It softens the sounds around you, gives your thoughts somewhere to rest and fills a room without demanding attention. Many listeners find that a few minutes of mountain wind help them settle into focused work, clear their head between tasks or simply breathe more slowly.


Because every episode lasts 10 to 13 minutes, Mountain Wind Sounds is made for the moments in between. Press play for a focused study session or a deep work sprint. Use it as a short work break when the office gets loud. Take a short nap with the mountain air in your ears, read a chapter with a howling summit wind in the background, or let the steady rhythm of the gusts guide a breathing exercise or a short meditation. Many listeners like to queue several episodes back to back, travelling from a soft valley breeze to a howling ridge and back again.


The wind changes from episode to episode: calm and whispering, steady and rushing, gusty and buffeting, or cold and howling across open rock. You will hear wind in different seasons and at different times of day, on bare stone and through alpine forest, out in the open and from the shelter of a mountain hut. What stays the same is the purity of the sound: real nature recordings, nothing synthesised, nothing added, nothing to break the spell.


If you love wind sounds, alpine ambience, high-altitude soundscapes, natural white noise or simply the feeling of standing somewhere high and open, follow Mountain Wind Sounds so new mountain winds arrive in your feed automatically. Put on your headphones, close your eyes and let the mountain air move around you.


Mountain wind sounds for focus, study, reading, calm, stress relief, breathing, meditation and short naps. No music. No ads. No interruptions.

title: Grace Actually
author: christopher lovell
description:
Grace Actually is a podcast about finding the grace of God in the middle of ordinary life - the good bits, the difficult bits and all the slightly chaotic bits in between.
The podcast grew out of Chris’s simple desire to slow down and pay attention. After years of rushing from one thing to the next, he started to wonder what might happen if he actually stopped to notice the moments where God was already present. 
Grace Actually began as a collection of reflections about faith, life, teaching, grief, change, joy and all the unexpected moments that make up our everyday stories. Now, those reflections are becoming a conversation.
Each episode begins with a story or moment from ordinary life - sometimes funny, sometimes difficult and sometimes a little bit of both. Chris explores what that moment might have to say about faith and where we might find God’s grace within it. From there, the conversation turns to Scripture, taking some time to reflect on what God might be saying through His Word before moving into a space for personal reflection, Lectio Divina and prayer.
So, whether you’re listening in the car, over your breakfast or somewhere in the middle of your day, come and join Chris for a little pause in the chaos. There’ll be honest reflections, real-life stories, faith, laughter and the occasional “well, I definitely didn’t see that coming!” moment.
Because grace doesn’t always arrive with fireworks or dramatic signs. Sometimes it’s found in the small things we might otherwise overlook in a conversation, a struggle, a change of plan, a moment of joy or even an ordinary Tuesday.
This is Grace Actually:a podcast hosted by Chris, about noticing the grace that is already there, right in the middle of real life. Because Grace Actually is all around.

title: Bus Tales
author: Ninja Productions
description:
It’s 2:14 a.m. and you’re the only passenger on the last bus out of town. The driver has worked this route for decades, and he knows things he won’t say in daylight.

Bus Tales is a horror podcast drawn from the folklore of Eastern Europe and the Nordic north. Each episode, the driver tells you what he’s seen from behind the wheel, or who he’s picked up at stops that aren’t on any map. The strzyga waiting by the cemetery gate. The rusalka who calls from the river. The draugr that won’t stay buried. The house spirit you forgot to leave bread for.

These are real legends, the kind people in Central Europe, the Balkans and the Nordics still don’t joke about after dark. 

Did it really happen? I don't know. People say all sorts of things when the night gets too quiet. Especially when they stare into the dark for too long. But the driver has been turning the wheel on these empty roads for thirty years. He has lived long enough to know that out there, past the streetlights... we are not always alone.

New episodes every Friday. Headphones on, lights off.

Next stop: nowhere.

https://buymeacoffee.com/bustales

Even people's thoughts and feelings are monitored.The main character, Winston Smith, works at the Ministry of Truth, where he changes historical records to match the Party's version of reality. However, Winston secretly hates the regime and dreams of freedom. When he falls in love with Julia, he begins to rebel against the system, risking his life.Through this novel, Orwell explores important themes such as the loss of freedom, the abuse of power, censorship and the manipulation of truth. 1984 is a powerful warning about the dangers of dictatorship and a society where individuals have no right to think freely. Despite being written many decades ago, its message remains relevant today.

Each episode is a seat at the table — a space to talk openly about where we come from, what we’ve lived through, what we believe, and what we’re building. Some conversations are deep. Some are light. Some are about faith, purpose, family, work, or failure. All of them are human. No shouting. No chasing trends. No pretending to have it all figured out. 
Real conversation. Real people. Real stories — At the Table
*Not affiliated with DoW.

title: A Paranarrative

description:
A Paranarrative explores the strange, the unsettling, and the moments where the world doesn’t behave the way it should.
Each episode focuses on a paranormal story — hauntings, folklore, encounters and experiences from around the world — told with calm, immersive narration and a focus on atmosphere.
Stories that stay with you long after they’re told.

title: CBSA Hiring Insider
author: joincbsa
description:
Learn how to join the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) and succeed in the hiring process. This podcast breaks down every step to becoming a Border Services Officer in Canada, including the application, exam, interview, polygraph, training, and salary.
Get clear, practical guidance to help you pass each stage and get hired faster.
Start here: https://joincbsa.ca

title: The Thought Line Show
author: Jessica Huns
description:
The Thought Line is an inside look at how remarkable people actually think, through doubt, loss, pivots and breakthroughs.
Host Jessica Huns maps each guest’s life into a timeline, then takes them back into the moments that shaped them to ask what most interviews skip: What were you thinking, and what got you to the next point?
Wherever you are on your own timeline, you’ll hear from someone who stood exactly where you’re standing, and how they found their way forward.

title: No Particular Point
author: Ethan, Kelsie, and Nance
description:
Welcome to No Particular Point, the podcast where conversations take unexpected turns, opinions are given whether anyone asked for them or not, and staying on topic is apparently a personal attack.
Join Ethan, Kelsie, and “Nance” as they tackle interesting topics, offer questionable wisdom, debate things that probably don't need debating, and wander down tangents so far removed from the original conversation that even they forget how they got there.
Three friends. Three microphones. Absolutely no guarantee of a point.
Our opinions are our own. All statements should not be considered factual

title: The Breaking Pointe Podcast

description: The Breaking Pointe Podcast explores the intersection of dance, health, medicine, and performance. Created by Chelsea Teel and Itamar Stern, the podcast brings together evidence-informed conversations with dancers, healthcare professionals, teachers, and industry experts to examine the challenges dancers face, challenge common misconceptions, and make dance medicine education more accessible. From injury prevention and rehabilitation to the culture and complexities of the dance world, we’re here to examine, educate, and evolve.

description:
Talent is overrated. The work behind it isn’t.
Untalented is the podcast that show talent is built, not given. I simply talk with athletes, actors, chefs, entrepreneurs and more about flops, routines and the grind behind the glory. 
Over a coffee, a croissant, and a bit of French humour.

title: The American Syllabus
author: Cameron Miles
description:
The American Syllabus 
*****
Every university in the United States has a glossy brochure showing sunny lawns and smiling students, but almost nobody explains how the system actually works on the inside. Welcome to The American Syllabus, hosted by veteran academic advisor Cameron Miles Hamilton. Whether you are an international student planning your move to an American campus, a parent trying to make sense of tuition numbers, or a first-year student figuring out how professors grade, this show gives you the verified ground truth. We skip the marketing myths to focus on what actually matters: choosing the right institution, cutting degree costs legally, picking majors with real career value, and thriving inside the American classroom.

description: Millennial Monsters is a paranormal mystery that follows Wendell Batty, a queer 32-year-old werewolf who just wants to live an ordinary life. But, when he's sent threatening letters and is framed for a string of supernatural murders, Wen teams up with his friends and the monster hunter who once tried to kill him to find answers. As he dodges the paranormal police, they embark on a dangerous and deadly adventure, discovering a shocking link that circles back to the Super Blood Moon in 1993 when Wen was first bitten.

title: The Holiness Standard
author: Tyler Gridley
description: Welcome to The Holiness Standard Podcast—where we get into God’s Word to uncover the truth about holiness and what it really means to live a life set apart. I’m your host, Tyler Gridley , and in each episode, we’ll talk with Godly men and women to learn how to live sanctified and holy in an un-Godly world. So if you desire the truth, want to live a separate life that’s pleasing to the Lord you're in the right place. Thank you for listening.

title: The Missing Manual for Your Marriage
author: kevonowenchristiancounseling
description:
The Missing Manual for Your Marriage
Do you and your partner find yourselves stuck in the same looping arguments, feeling misunderstood, or slowly drifting into a flat "roommates" dynamic?
Welcome to The Missing Manual for Your Marriage, hosted by licensed clinical psychotherapist and Christian counselor Dr. Kevon Owen. In this podcast, we unpack the reality that 69% of relationship conflicts are completely perpetual, and teach you how to start talking about them better.
Each episode provides practical, evidence-based communication skills—including active listening, "I" statements, and the art of fast, specific repair—to replace blame with understanding. We also explore simple, daily "rituals of connection," transition routines to protect your home from work-life stress, and healthy ways to handle in-law tension.
Thoughtfully blending empirically grounded clinical methods with faith-informed wisdom, this show is designed to help you stop battling each other and start building a safer, more intimate life together.

author: The Democracy Forum
description:
Time to Question | A Podcast by The Democracy Forum

In a world of rapidly changing politics, emerging technologies and shifting global challenges, asking the right questions has never been more important.

Time to Question, a podcast from The Democracy Forum (TDF), brings together leading experts, academics, policymakers and influential voices to explore the issues shaping our world.

Through thought-provoking conversations, informed analysis and open debate, we examine the challenges and opportunities facing democracy, international relations, technology and global society.

From the growing influence of artificial intelligence on politics and democracy to the complex issues defining our future, each episode offers fresh perspectives, meaningful discussion and the opportunity to question established thinking.

Different perspectives. Important conversations. Time to Question.

Presented by The Democracy Forum (TDF).

title: History on Repeat
author: Andrae Murphy
description:
History isn't just about dates and names. It's about the stories, decisions, triumphs, and mistakes that continue to shape our world today. On History on Repeat, we dive into fascinating moments from the past and uncover how history echoes through modern events, culture, politics, technology, and everyday life.
Designed for students, curious minds, and lifelong learners, each episode breaks down complex historical topics into engaging conversations that are easy to understand and fun to explore. From ancient civilizations and world-changing inventions to famous leaders, conflicts, and cultural movements, we'll discover why the past matters and how it continues to repeat itself in surprising ways.
Because the best way to understand the future is to learn from the past.

description: Welcome to The Right to Yap! Hosted by University of Iowa Turning Point USA President Kayleigh Jurczyk and Vice President Isaac Branch, we dive into politics, campus culture, current events, and everything in between. title: The Soft Voice
author: revampednative
description:
Hey there, I’m Shae, and welcome to Soft Voice, Hard Truth.

I’m a Gen X woman with a lifetime of stories, a few hard-earned lessons, and a whole lot left to say.

This is a place where we pull up a chair and have real, honest conversations about life, love, relationships, healing, and rediscovering ourselves in the second half of life.

We’ll laugh, we might cry, and occasionally, we’re going to say the things everybody else is thinking but nobody wants to say out loud!

Because getting older doesn’t mean our stories are over. Sometimes, it means we’re finally finding the courage to tell them.

So grab your coffee, pull up a chair, and join me.

We’ve got some things to talk about.

And remember, you can have a soft voice and still speak a hard truth.

title: Salt and Stories
author: Zilin Ding
description:
Somewhere along the way, we learned how to put our lives in order, but became worse at lingering in it. 
We eat, but rarely remember the taste of a meal. We pass through our kitchen, no longer pausing for the warmth rising from a pot. We sit down to write, and our minds go blank.
Salt & Stories begins here.
We begin with food, following it into memory and writing. For sometimes, writing is not about creating a story, but finding our way back to ones there all along.
A bowl of soup, emptied without a thought. A dinner we were certain we’d forget. Perhaps that is enough to write a life.

title: Waiting for Elon
author: Mary Stompe
description:
Waiting for Elon is a feature-length audio documentary currently in development that explores the devastating emotional impact of online celebrity romance scams—not only on victims, but also on the families who desperately try to help them.
The documentary is told through my perspective as the sister of a woman who believes she is in a relationship with someone claiming to be Elon Musk. Over the course of more than two years, I documented our conversations, her growing emotional investment, and my family's attempts to understand, support, and protect her.

title: Behind the Scenes With Amaka
author: Amaka Okolobi
description: Behind the Scenes with Amaka is a space for honest conversations about heartbreak, healing, relationships, emotional well-being, and self-growth. I sit down with therapists, doctors, life coaches, and other experts to explore the struggles we often face but don’t always talk about. Whether you’re healing, trying to understand yourself, or simply looking for comfort and clarity, this podcast reminds you that you’re not alone. Because there’s always more happening behind the scenes
